title: Console Audit: Query Journeys, Saved Playlists, and Flexible Export Paths
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary:
Implement a user-centric Audit Console feature set that lets admins and security engineers build, save, and replay complex audit query journeys ("playlists"), apply multi-faceted filters with cursor-based pagination, and export result sets in CSV or newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON). This ticket covers the end-to-end flow: query builder UX, server-side query translation, role-aware result filtering per RBAC v2, export backpressure/throttling, and saved-playlist storage and sharing semantics.

Background and motivation:
Our current audit viewer supports basic filters and small-range exports, but customers are asking for: saved queries that can be shared between teams, repeatable query sequences (e.g., pivot -> drill -> timeframe) for incident investigations, reliable large exports (NDJSON for SIEM ingestion), and RBAC-aware search results so restricted users never see redacted fields. This also ties into SSO/SAML-driven admin controls; saved playlists should only be visible to users with the right scope.

User stories:
- As an org admin, I can create a saved playlist (sequence of queries) and share it with a team so incident responders can re-run the same investigation steps.
- As a security analyst, I can search audit logs using compound filters (actor, action, resource type, time window) and page through results with stable cursors.
- As a compliance engineer, I can export a filtered result set as NDJSON (for SIEM) or CSV (for spreadsheets), and the export can be resumed/retried if it times out.
- As an operator, I can configure per-customer export quotas and see export job status in the console.

Technical approach / design decisions:
- Query & filter model: server will accept a canonical JSON query AST translated into underlying storage queries. The frontend will build that AST via the query builder. Avoid ad-hoc query strings to improve auditability and caching.
- Pagination: use cursor-based pagination (opaque cursor) for forward/backward navigation and stable results under live ingestion. Each cursor encodes sort key + request snapshot timestamp.
- Exports: two modes: quick export (table-size < 10k rows) streamed synchronously as CSV/NDJSON; background export for large jobs (asynchronous export job stored in S3 with signed URL). Background export will surface a job status endpoint with retry/backoff.
- RBAC v2 integration: apply field-level redaction and row-level access checks at query execution time. Saved playlists must carry a minimal ACL: visibility (private/org/team) and allow-list of roles.
- Saved playlists storage: in core config DB with encrypted metadata and owner pointers. Shared playlists will be discoverable via a listing API with RBAC enforcement.
- Throttling & quotas: reuse existing rate-limiting infra; add an export-specific token bucket per-org.
- Security: saved playlists cannot embed ephemeral credentials. SAML/SSO group mappings control team-level visibility.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Frontend: query builder can construct compound filters and save a playlist with a name/description; saved playlist can be listed and loaded.
2) Pagination: results can be paged using opaque cursors; cursors survive small ingestion windows and preserve order.
3) Export: small sync exports download as CSV/NDJSON; large exports create a background job with signed download URL that expires.
4) RBAC: users without view scope cannot see redacted fields; shared playlists obey ACLs.
5) Admin controls: console shows per-org active export jobs, success/fail counts, and allows manual cancel.
6) Tests: unit & integration tests cover query AST translation, cursor correctness, export job lifecycle, and RBAC checks.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Cursor snapshot staleness: do we snapshot the query time window (strong consistency) or accept eventual consistency for lower latency? Proposal: snapshot timestamp for cursor generation with a TTL of 2 minutes to balance correctness vs throughput.
- Export format for complex nested events: CSV flattens but loses nested context. Use NDJSON as canonical export for programmatic ingestion; CSV remains for simple tables.
- Saved playlist sharing model: should owners be able to pin a playlist org-wide? For now, support private/team/org scopes, but require an explicit "promote to org" approval by an admin.

Implementation plan / checklist:
- [ ] API: POST /audit/queries/compile -> return AST + estimated size (ENG-77321-API)
- [ ] API: GET /audit/results?cursor=... implement stable cursor semantics (ENG-77321-PAG)
- [ ] API: POST /audit/exports (sync/async) -> export job object (ENG-77321-EXPORT)
- [ ] DB: saved_playlists table with ACL metadata and owner references (ENG-77321-SAVE)
- [ ] Frontend: query builder UX, playlist create/list/load flows (ENG-77321-UX)
- [ ] RBAC: hook into RBAC v2 enforcement for field/row redaction (ENG-77321-RBAC)
- [ ] Observability: metrics for export job durations, failure reasons; alert on repeated failures (ENG-77321-METRICS)
- [ ] Docs: Console help for saved playlists and export sizes/limits (PM/Docs)

Rollout plan:
- Alpha behind feature flag for internal security and SRE teams (2 weeks)
- Beta opt-in for early customers with export quotas limited to 5 concurrent jobs
- Gradual enablement for all orgs with default quotas and admin controls visible in Console

2025-02-28 - Security (Rohit Patel): Security review: flagged saved_playlists metadata encryption and ensured SAML group mapping used for team visibility. Recommended explicit audit entry when playlist ACL changes. Added as follow-up task.
